Wayne Gretzky.text: Has more assists than any other player has total career points.
Wayne Gretzky.evidence: Gretzky is the leading career point scorer and assist producer in NHL history and has more assists than any other player has total career points.

Jaromir Jagr.text: Was the NHL's youngest player at 18 in 1990, and later its oldest, at 45.
Jaromir Jagr.evidence: In 1990, at age 18, he was the youngest player in the NHL. Until his transfer, at age 45, he was the oldest player in the NHL and is the oldest player to record a hat-trick.

Mark Messier.text: The last active player in any major North American league to have played in the 1970s.
Mark Messier.evidence: He was the last WHA player to be active in professional ice hockey and the last active player in any of the major North American professional sports leagues to have played in the 1970s.

Gordie Howe.text: Became the oldest person to play in an NHL game, retiring weeks after turning 52.
Gordie Howe.evidence: By playing in the opening game on October 11, he became the oldest person to play in an NHL game and appeared in all 80 games of the season, scoring 15 goals. Weeks after turning 52 years old, Howe retired.

Ron Francis.text: Was hired in 2019 as the first general manager of the Seattle Kraken.
Ron Francis.evidence: On July 18, 2019, he was hired as the first general manager of the Seattle Kraken.

Marcel Dionne.text: His 77 points as a rookie set the record for a player's first NHL season.
Marcel Dionne.evidence: His 77 points in his rookie season set the record for most points for a player in their first NHL season.

Sidney Crosby.text: The youngest player, and only teenager, to win a scoring title in any major North American sports league.
Sidney Crosby.evidence: By his second season, he led the NHL with 120 points to capture the Art Ross Trophy, becoming the youngest player and the only teenager to win a scoring title in any major North American sports league.

Steve Yzerman.text: In 2002 he won both an Olympic gold medal and the Stanley Cup.
Steve Yzerman.evidence: Yzerman led the Wings to five first-place regular season finishes and three Stanley Cup championships (1997, 1998, and 2002). ... In 2002, Yzerman won an Olympic gold medal, making him one of few players to win an Olympic gold medal and the Stanley Cup in the same year.

Mario Lemieux.text: The only player to score a goal in each of the five possible situations in a single NHL game.
Mario Lemieux.evidence: He is the only player to score a goal in each of the five possible situations in a single NHL game, a feat he accomplished in 1988.

Alexander Ovechkin.text: Holds the NHL record for scoring on the most individual goalies.
Alexander Ovechkin.evidence: He also holds multiple other NHL records, including the most power play goals, most goals in away games, most overtime goals, most game-winning goals, most individual goalies scored upon, and most goals with one team.
